why: the first run (job run 436369232677286) ran out of memory and wrote no results; its log showed seed 0 outside the original absolute tolerances, which turned out to be below PyTorch's own batch-size noise. Owner's decision, option (a), recorded in PLAN's decisions log

unchanged.models: the shipped EfficientNet-B0 v2 checkpoints, seeds 0 to 2 (results/phase2/overnight/v2/final_models.json in the volume), each checked by weight hash
unchanged.export: torch.onnx.export with dynamo, outputs features (1,280-d penultimate) and logits, dynamic batch 1 to 1,024; one file per seed; the ensemble is the mean of the three softmax outputs, computed outside the graph as in Phase 2
unchanged.parity_images: 512 validation images (positions drawn with numpy default_rng(0) from the clients' validation split), evaluation transform: resize 224, centre crop, ImageNet normalisation. No test image is used

latency.where: Databricks serverless CPU (the job's machine; Render's free tier is not measured here)
latency.what: one image (batch 1), already preprocessed; PyTorch eval with no_grad against ONNX Runtime CPUExecutionProvider; per seed and for the 3-model ensemble
latency.how: 50 untimed warm-up calls, then 300 timed calls; p50 and p95 in milliseconds; thread counts and CPU count recorded

outputs.repo: results/phase3/onnx/results.json: parity, latency, versions, file hashes and sizes

noise_measured_by: results/phase3/onnx/noise.json (job run 540132085766008): PyTorch at batch 1 against batch 32, same 512 validation images and weights; no ONNX

rule.statement: ONNX Runtime and PyTorch both at batch 32: every gap (logits, probabilities, relative features; ensemble probabilities) at most 2x PyTorch's own noise above, and a top-class disagreement only on an image where PyTorch also disagrees with itself or the top two class probabilities are within 0.01
rule.run_once: the parity check runs once under this spec; a miss is recorded and fails the job
